title: How I Make 3D Game Assets with AI: Claude, Nano Banana, Meshy, & Unity
author: nosark

comments.author: Odd-Woodpecker-592
comments.body: I'd love some advice on this too.  I'm working on a 3D space fighter FPS right now.  Between Claude just spinning some effects together for me and this resource, [https://opengameart.org/](https://opengameart.org/) I've been putting stuff together but it's a struggle!

replies.author: nosark
replies.body: I do all of my modeling using meshy using the process in the post. Have you tried using an AI model generator?

replies.author: Odd-Woodpecker-592
replies.body: I have not yet.  Honestly I'm not that creative so I've been relying on the creativity of others willing to share.  I can see good assets and put them together but building assets on my own is kind of out of my wheelhouse.  Though I've heard good things about Meshy so maybe I'll give that a spin.  Thanks for the advice!

replies.author: nosark
replies.body:
I would iterate with Claude or chat gpt to create a prompt do the object you want to feed to something like nano banana. Then give that to meshy.

You can have Claude describe the object on a solid background specifically for 3D generation.

replies.author: Odd-Woodpecker-592
replies.body: I'll give that a shot.  Appreciate your feedback!

comments.author: TheSpriteWizard
comments.body: Bruh. My Meshy models always have Mesh Drag. It’s pretty bad. How do you fix that in blender?

replies.author: nosark
replies.body: What is mesh drag? I've not fixed anything, so I'm not sure if I have it or I've just ignored it.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: It’s when the model morphs the mesh in strange ways after rigging. It happens in both the Meshy app and when exporting the GLB/FLX into other software such as blender.

replies.author: nosark
replies.body: I don't use their animations yet (mixamo for bipeds, and a few custom animations) and I mostly have relied on very simple animations in my game where it hadn't been a visible problem.

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: If I understand you correctly, you mean mesh deformation because of bad skin weights. When the mesh “stretches” where it shouldn’t. The usual fix is weight painting cleanup. That means you need to check which bones in your rig affect wrong vertices, remove wrong influences and normalize the weights
